about: Spacecraft in orbit around other worlds: periapsis and apoapsis altitude (km), inclination (deg). Orbits are drawn from these published values with an arbitrary orientation of the node and an arbitrary starting point; the period is worked out from the altitudes. Positions along the orbit are illustrative, not tracked.

moon.name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter
moon.note: Mapping the Moon since 2009; its camera and laser altimeter made the maps this atlas uses.

moon.name: Chandrayaan-2 orbiter
moon.note: India’s lunar orbiter; its lander Vikram was lost on landing, the orbiter carries on.

moon.name: Queqiao-2
moon.note: Relay satellite for the far side (Chang’e 6 and later).

mars.name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
mars.note: Carries HiRISE, the sharpest camera at Mars.

mars.name: MAVEN
mars.note: Studies the upper atmosphere and how Mars lost its air.

mars.name: ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter
mars.note: Sniffs trace gases such as methane; relays for the rovers.

mars.name: Tianwen-1 orbiter
mars.note: China’s first Mars orbiter; it delivered the Zhurong rover.

mars.name: Hope (Al-Amal)
mars.note: A high orbit that watches the whole atmosphere through the day.

venus.name: Akatsuki
venus.note: Studied Venus’s winds from orbit; contact was lost in 2024.

mercury.name: BepiColombo MPO
mercury.note: Due to enter orbit in late 2026; this is its planned orbit.

mercury.name: BepiColombo Mio
mercury.note: Due to enter orbit in late 2026; this is its planned orbit.

jupiter.name: Juno
jupiter.note: Dives close over the poles every 33 days.

ceres.name: Dawn
ceres.note: Mission ended in 2018; it stays in orbit, silent.
